biography.plain_text: Saddam Hussein was an Iraqi Ba'athist politician and authoritarian president who ruled Iraq from 1979 until his overthrow in 2003. Rising through the party after the 1968 coup, he centralised power around a repressive state apparatus. His presidency encompassed wars with Iran and Kuwait, international sanctions, and systematic abuses against Iraqis.

long_biography.plain_text:
The Ba'ath Party's return to power in 1968 gave Saddam Hussein the machinery through which he became Iraq's dominant political figure. As vice-president he controlled security institutions and accumulated authority before replacing Ahmed Hassan al-Bakr as president in 1979. He then concentrated rule around the presidency, party and security services.

His government launched the Iran-Iraq War and invaded Kuwait, bringing prolonged conflict and international sanctions. State repression targeted political opponents and Kurdish and Shia communities. Overthrown by the United States-led invasion, he was captured later that year. An Iraqi court convicted him of crimes against humanity for the killings at Dujail, and he was executed three years later.

uncertainties.detail: Forbes published matching wealth reporting, but exact-name, profile-domain and direct profile-path checks did not produce a dedicated person profile. The status is not_found and no Forbes social link is proposed.

28 April 1937 was the official and widely reported birth date, but the exact date was not contemporaneously recorded and later accounts place his birth within a wider range. The full Arabic name also uses patronymic elements rather than a Western middle-name and surname structure. Birth fields and middle_names therefore remain unchanged rather than presenting disputed or culturally misleading segmentation as certain.
The owner record gives 10 December 2006, while every strong source reviewed records his execution and death on 30 December 2006. A correction to death_day 30 is proposed with very-high confidence.

Forbes and Treasury evidence support an energy-sector origin through diverted oil revenue and smuggling, but investigators could not cleanly separate personal, family, regime and Iraqi government assets. Wealth origin and relationship remain Unknown; the dossier does not treat state oil reserves or office-held resources as private property.

Published prose is limited to durable, directly relevant features of his public record: authoritarian rule, regional wars, repression, overthrow, conviction and execution. It excludes vessel facts, graphic detail, contemporary partisan comparison and disputed personal-fortune figures.

No verified personal social account or personal website was appropriate for the deceased subject. Wikipedia is proposed as the only exact-person profile. The active Head of state tag is assigned; Oil & gas is omitted because governing a state petroleum economy and diverting state revenue do not establish the private operating mandate required by that tag.
